title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: ongoing effort to reduce per-token unit economics while preserving latency and quality. This PR wires together three related pieces: 1) safer defaults for continuous batching and response-prefix/KV caching, 2) model quantization profile selection and rollout metadata, and 3) a small console + CLI surface to surface unit-econ estimates for routes/models so SRE/product can make informed choices. Motivation: customers running high-throughput chat workloads had high unit cost variability; previous experiments showed gains from smarter defaults + quant recommendations but required manual tuning. This automates the common paths and exposes the tuning knobs.
commits: b1a2c3: runtime: add autotune scoring module (latency/cost tradeoff) + tests

a7b8c9: model-registry: add quant_profiles metadata and selection heuristics
e9f8d7: console: unit-econ widget + CLI report command
f1e2d3: docs: add guide and migration notes for defaults
review_comments: Liam Chen: Overall looks good. Two requests: (1) add a short-circuit that bypasses autotune for pinned routes, (2) add load-simulation unit test to catch regressions.
Author (Aisha Patel): Added short-circuit and load-sim test in commits d4e5f6 and tests/integration. See updated test that covers pinned route behavior.
Marta Ruiz: Quant profile selection should prefer FP16 on GPU-backed dedicated instances. Please ensure registry metadata includes supported accel types.
Author: Updated model-registry/quant_profiles.json to include accelerator hints and a deterministic selection fallback.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky canary retried once; stable after fix)
bench/perf: pass (end-to-end canary shows ~12% unit-cost reduction; initial 3% latency regression at 8k seq fixed by concurrency cap tweak)
release_notes:
- Autotune: safer defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching to improve unit economics out-of-the-box.
- Model registry: quantization profiles added and automatically suggested based on workload and accelerator.
- Console/CLI: unit-econ estimates per-route/model for faster ops decisions.
- No breaking changes; pinned routes continue to bypass autotune by default.
performance_summary: Canary results: median per-token cost down 12% on standard chat workload (95% CI 10-14%). Latency p50/p95 within 2% of baseline after tuning caps. Quant profiles yield additional 6-8% cost on dedicated GPU workloads with negligible quality impact in evaled prompts.
testing_instructions: Run integration tests locally: pytest tests/integration/test_batching_cache.py::test_pinned_route_bypass and pytest tests/integration/test_batching_cache.py::test_load_simulation (these emulate 1000 concurrent short requests). To reproduce canary: deploy deploy/k8s/autotune-configmap.yaml to staging and run canary job (scripts/canary/run_unit_econ.sh).
notes: Follow-up work: add per-tenant autotune thresholds, telemetry for quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets (ENG-9922).
